description: brave-core: a Chromium-derived checkout built with pnpm, gtest binaries, and chromium_src overrides.
research: Read {bestPractices} to identify which best practice sub-documents apply, then read those sub-documents
validations: Commit changes, then run the /review skill from the target repo in a fresh subagent (read .claude/skills/review/SKILL.md and follow Local Mode steps); report all findings back to the main context; fix any violations and commit the fixes (must pass)
Run pnpm run format one final time; if it makes any changes, amend the last commit with the formatting fixes

testSteps.testFix: Run the test: {testBinary} --gtest_filter={testFilter} (must pass - run 5 times to verify consistency, unless this is a filter file change only)
testSteps.disabledTest: Run the test: {testBinary} --gtest_filter={testFilter} (must pass - run 5 times to verify consistency)
testSteps.generic: Find and run relevant tests to verify the change (must pass)

judged.risk/funds: The change can move, lose, expose or miscount a user's money or keys: the crypto wallet, key and seed handling, swaps, bridges, transaction signing, Rewards payouts, or payments and subscriptions.
judged.risk/security: The change touches a security boundary: IPC and Mojo interfaces between processes, the sandbox, permission and origin checks, URL or input validation and parsing, cryptography, authentication, or the handling of credentials and secrets.
judged.risk/privacy-promises-affected: The change can alter something Brave tells users it does for their privacy: Shields blocking, fingerprinting protections, storage and cookie partitioning, telemetry and P3A, what data is sent and to whom, or how long data is kept.
judged.risk/network-calls: The change adds or alters a network request: a new URL, endpoint or fetcher, a change to the headers, cookies or body sent, or a change to which server receives them.
